gaps.note: cut to close up of lure

stage_a.note: The founders deliver a highly energetic and positive pitch.
They show great excitement when pointing to the investors.
They are friendly and approachable, though very focused on the product features.

venture.description: Robotic, rechargeable fishing lures that mimic the swimming patterns of real fish.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, and demonstrate their robotic, rechargeable fishing lure.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about how much can be learned on the show.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the product is different from anything they have ever used to fish with.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz confirms he has never seen anything like it and explains the typical issues with traditional lures.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how long the lure holds a charge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz states the battery life for the different sizes, ranging from 45 minutes to up to two hours.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert questions what makes the founders fish experts and why he should believe them.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan explains that he works as a project manager at manufacturing facilities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz adds that he is a licensed professional counselor working in community mental health.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert jokes that their professions make perfect sense for their business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan shares a personal story about fishing with his father and the sacrifices his parents made as immigrants.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks where they immigrated from.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan and Kanz reply that they are from Iran.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks about the costs to make the lures, the retail prices, and their total sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz states the landed price for the mini is eight dollars and the classic is ten dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what the new large lure costs to make.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz gives the cost for the large lure and details the retail prices for all three sizes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if their sales are all direct to consumer or if they are in retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz explains that the majority of sales are on their website, with some in small stores and a Canadian distributor.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks about their presence in large retail stores like Bass Pro Shops.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan replies that they are hoping to make a deal with the investors to help open those retail doors.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin notes the high valuation implied by their ask and asks about their sales to justify it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz states their sales for the current year to date and their projections for the rest of the year and next.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks if the company is currently making money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz confirms they are, noting they both work full time, have zero debt, and funded the start themselves.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori comments that they didn't mess around.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz states they haven't taken a penny out of the company and reinvest everything they earn.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks if they own the company equally.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz confirms they own the company equally.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin suggests they should sell the product as an aquarium toy instead of a fishing lure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori laughs and adds that you wouldn't have to feed the robotic fish.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark suggests it could be used at a restaurant.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert agrees that it is a good idea.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark states he is out because he is not a fisherman, despite thinking it is a clever product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori exits, citing that she is not a fisherman and feels the business is too early for her.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin argues they are just a product right now and challenges them on how he would get his money back.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz deflects the question by saying business is about who you know, referencing the sharks' connections.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin challenges their logic, pointing out that if he invests and does the work, their valuation is too high.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori notes that Kevin is setting up a royalty deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin playfully asks Lori if she mentioned a royalty deal.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan reacts with amusement to the impending royalty offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin makes an offer involving a royalty until he recoups a million dollars, plus equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert tells the founders that Kevin's offer is a great one.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert exits, stating he disagrees with their view on connections and feels the business isn't for him.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan thanks Robert for his feedback.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond exits, explaining he would need too much equity to justify the distribution work required.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz thanks Daymond.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin points out he is the only remaining option and asks for their decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz counters Kevin's offer with a request for more money and a higher equity stake.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori interjects to ask what the royalty would be in their counteroffer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz clarifies that their counteroffer includes no royalty.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin expresses disbelief at their counteroffer, implying it is unrealistic.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin breaks down the counter, arguing it asks him to give more money with no clear return path.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz explains they made the counter because they are young and seeking guidance.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin tells them to listen when they have an investor and not to make foolish counters.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori pushes the founders to decide if they want Kevin and will accept a royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz asks to briefly discuss with his partner before making another counter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz counters with lower royalty terms and a lower cap.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin rejects the revised counteroffer as unattractive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz asks if they can lower the equity component of the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin withdraws his offer and states he is out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert remarks that they had a deal but failed to close it.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan laments that they priced themselves too high.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin re-enters, offering his original terms as a final chance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders quickly whisper to each other to make a decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz accepts Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond jokes about how Kevin managed to revive the dead deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin boasts about his negotiating skills.

decisions.note: He is not a fisherman so he drops out.
She is not a fisherman and feels it is too early.

decisions.terms: $325k for 10% equity, $3 per unit royalty until $1M is paid
decisions.note: Suggests a royalty structure to ensure he gets his money back.
Disagrees with their approach to networking and feels it isn't for him.
The valuation is too high for the amount of work required.
Counters asking for more money and no royalty.

decisions.terms: $325k for 10% equity, $1.50 per unit royalty until $500k is paid
decisions.note: Counters to lower the royalty amount and cap.
Asks if they can reduce the equity given.
Refuses the final counter and pulls his offer.

decisions.terms: $325k for 10% equity, $3 per unit royalty until $1M is paid
decisions.note: Comes back in with his exact original terms as a final offer.

record.notes: The pitch features high energy and several negotiation twists at the end.
